newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican pension funds spent 1.29 bln pesos in ads.
newsitem.headline: Mexican pension funds spent 1.29 bln pesos in ads.

text.p: Mexico's new private pension funds spent 1.29 billion pesos on advertising between February and May, Reforma newspaper said on Wednesday.

The newspaper cited publicity firm IBOPE as saying that Afore Garante spent the most on advertizing during the period, about 253.95 million pesos. Garante is a joint venture between Grupo Financiero Serfin, Citibank and AFP Habitat. Grupo Financiero Bancomer followed with advertizing spending of 210.17 million pesos and Afore Previnter, comprised of Boston AIG Co and The Bank of Nova Scotia spent 184.92 million pesos.
Ads for the nation's new pension fund system have barraged television and radio and signs urging people to join compete for space along freeways with election campaign posters.

IBOPE also calculated the cost of publicity per worker signed up with the funds. The pension fund of local insurance company Tepeyac SA spent the most, 10,825 pesos on advertising for each worker signed up.

The pension funds, known as afores, which IBOPE said spent the least on advertizing per worker were: Afore Zurich of Zurich Vida, Profuturo GNP -- composed of Grupo Nacional Provincial, Provida Internacional and Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, the government's Siglo XXI and the pension fund of Grupo Financiero Banorte.
